# A combined foundation for shared generation

5 October 2026. Integration of the existing programme, moral cultivation, and a newly certified joint process.

**The constructed combined process is now certified under its declared conditions, and the general characterization covers processes that change their own controllers and evaluators.** This closes the previous gap between individually demonstrated modules and one process that actually connects inquiry, judgment, execution, maintenance, and succession. The broader foundation also incorporates conscience, relationships, institutional power, and the revision of commitments, while keeping their substantive evidence distinct from the mathematical certificate.

The intended scope is a theory of how possibilities and capacities are formed, sustained, damaged, corrected, and transmitted—including when a process should end. It does not require every process to survive, every action to innovate, or every situation to need inquiry.

## The integrated root

The central proposition is:

> What happens changes the conditions of what can happen next. For agents and institutions, this includes changes to how they notice, remember, judge, choose, authorize, and teach. Shared generation asks whether those changes preserve and develop the conditions under which affected beings can live, respond, and form value.

This proposition organizes several kinds of work that can now be connected precisely:

| Part of the foundation | Its substantive question | Its current basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distinctions and dependencies | Which differences alter possible actions or consequences? What belongs inside the relevant boundary? | Existing faithful-representation and dependency-closure results; include hidden guards, shared disturbances, and permissions. |
| Material continuation | Can the actual process pay, act, maintain its capacities, and renew required support? | Resource and access theorems, actual transition models, and the new joint certificate. |
| Psychological formation | How do attention, emotion, memory, practice, and social experience shape later judgment? | The supplied traditions contribute mechanism descriptions and rival explanations; specific causal laws require evidence in the relevant setting. |
| Conscience and ethical direction | Whose harms, needs, and possibilities must count? How can judgment correct itself? | The already adopted [normative core](conscience-and-morality-core.md): fallible conscience and publicly defended commitments to shared generation. |
| Relationships and institutions | Who can be heard, refuse, authorize, act, challenge a rule, and obtain repair? | Explicit authority and intervention interfaces; consequences assessed beyond the operator's own success score. |
| Succession and self-revision | Can acquired knowledge and revised judgment survive replacement? Can the rules themselves change responsibly? | Actual archive/training/handoff in the new model; changing code, evaluators, and commitments within the general theorem. |

These roles need not appear identically in every system. A cell can instantiate resource use, feedback, and reproduction without conscience. A person's habits and a government's appeal procedure can share a functional question while having different mechanisms. A cancerous process can expand locally while destroying wider conditions of life. That is a substantive scale conflict the foundation should explain.

The structural boundary is chosen by the consequences and interventions under investigation. Existing results show how to retain the dependencies needed for an exact description. Where a finite quotient preserves observations, permissions, protected outcomes, progress, and action-dependent transitions, the prior [completeness bridge](completeness-bridge.md) transfers the relevant policy conclusions in both directions. Merely calling two situations “feedback” does not establish that correspondence.

## What the traditions add

Their contribution reaches beyond repair financing. They direct attention to the **formation of the decision maker**, including dispositions that shape which facts and people are even recognized.

Mencius describes nourishment and repeated loss of moral capacities; Xunzi emphasizes deliberate formation through learning and practice and disputes Mencius's explanation. Both belong in the framework without making their theories of human nature identical. [Mencius, Gaozi I](https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E5%AD%9F%E5%AD%90/%E5%91%8A%E5%AD%90%E4%B8%8A); [Xunzi, Xing e](https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E8%8D%80%E5%AD%90/%E6%80%A7%E6%83%A1%E7%AF%87).

The Gita supplies an ordered account connecting attention, attachment, anger, disturbed recollection, and judgment. AN 3.69 connects harmful dispositions with domination and refusal to acknowledge facts. These suggest distinct causal links to investigate rather than one undifferentiated variable called badness. [Gita 2.62](https://www.holy-bhagavad-gita.org/chapter/2/verse/62/), [2.63](https://www.holy-bhagavad-gita.org/chapter/2/verse/63/); [AN 3.69](https://accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/an/an03/an03.069.than.html).

The Catholic account explicitly connects repeated conduct, impaired judgment, and social structures that encourage further wrongdoing. The Qur'anic passage links moral orientation with cultivation and corruption, while supplying less of a stepwise mechanism. These remain theological accounts as well as materials for functional comparison. [Catechism 1865–1869](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_three/section_one/chapter_one/article_8/v_the_proliferation_of_sin.html); [Qur'an 91:7–10](https://legacy.quran.com/91/7-10).

Freida J. Jacques's Good Mind account connects attention and choice with working through hurt, including the danger of suppressing feelings. The Onondaga Nation describes governance through ordered deliberation and reconsideration with responsibility toward future generations. This brings interpersonal and institutional conditions into the account of cultivation. [Jacques's essay](https://peacecouncil.net/2025/01/15/january-2025-discipline-of-the-good-mind/); [Onondaga government](https://www.onondaganation.org/government/).

The resulting common research structure is:

**Experience and support → attention and interpretation → judgment and conduct → relationships and institutions → the conditions of subsequent experience and judgment.**

Cultivation can intervene throughout this loop. Better concentration alone might train obedience; truthful recognition might lack authority to act; anger might expose a real injury. Consequently, the relevant test is whether the practice improves warranted recognition and response while respecting affected parties. The [source-based companion](cultivation-and-shared-generation.md) preserves these countercases and ontological differences. Textual convergence supports this mechanism catalogue; it does not supply independent experimental replications or a single established psychology for everyone.

## The combined-process theorem

Let a configuration record the actual environment, installed programs, memories, available evidence, evaluators, commitments, permissions, resources, and succession state. Every transition includes the installed process's actual behavior and all admitted environmental outcomes. No hypothetical better controller is substituted when the installed controller fails.

Let **K** be the stated protection requirements and **E₁,…,E_q** the actual outcomes required to recur. Then, for an arbitrary set of configurations:

> Every admitted execution remains in K and delivers every required E infinitely often **if and only if** the reachable process lies in a safe closed region and, for each E, admits a well-founded rank that strictly decreases on every transition that does not deliver E.

A well-founded rank cannot decrease forever. An indefinitely deferred outcome would require precisely such an impossible descent. Closure supplies protection throughout the intervening steps. Conversely, if every actual execution is protected and each outcome recurs, the reachable region and ordinal ranks exist. This is an exact semantic characterization, not a promise of a terminating algorithm for arbitrary programs.

The usable certificate proves the conditions on actual component transitions: initial resources and competence, dispatch, evidence acquisition, formation, checking, admission, execution, replenishment, maintenance, training, handoff, and permitted revision. They share one resource account and one treatment of interference. Mutual support is legitimate when an initial base and every succeeding transition are verified; merely assuming that each component will rescue the others is insufficient.

The state set may be infinite. Code, representations, evaluators, and even the procedure for revising commitments may change. Those changes must satisfy the same joint contract. The theorem needs no external actor continually choosing an ideal policy. Its interpretation and admitted mechanisms still have to be specified correctly.

For continuing physical activity, elapsed time must diverge. For finite duties, rest, refusal, or exit, use the appropriate completion or request-resolution condition. Infinite recurring service is one specification, not the definition of every good life. The [full proof](combined-process-proof.md) treats these cases and separates all-path guarantees from probability-one progress.

## One actual process now satisfies the certificate

The new executable witness has a hidden response law over two contexts. It acquires paid observations, constructs a candidate from the linked records, buys fresh checks, revises a failing simplicity-first evaluator to prioritize fit, installs a validated program, performs ordinary service, and pays to archive and teach its program and evaluator to a successor.

Each of 23 microsteps costs one token before its effects occur. Productive auxiliary work supplies later receipts to the same capped account. The environment can switch to any different response law between periods. The controller cannot read that hidden law; calibration supplies its observations. Harm is assessed separately and persists despite later changes to the evaluator.

Exact enumeration finds **486 reachable states and 506 transitions**. Every baseline prefix is protected. The minimum account balance is two tokens at state boundaries and one immediately after payment. All six required outcomes—corrective installation, correct service in each context, archive maintenance, training, and competent handoff—occur at least once in every 23 transitions on every admitted infinite execution.

The initial evaluator actually changes, and the successor receives its archived replacement. Continual rewriting is unnecessary once the evaluator works. Knowledge, acceptance, installation, delivered response, and competent succession are separately checked events.

| Intervention in the model | Protection preserved? | Correct service in both contexts recurs on every run? | Competent succession recurs? |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Baseline | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Remove linked discovery records | Yes | No | Yes |
| Block ordinary execution | Yes | No | Yes |
| Remove renewal receipts | Yes | No | No |
| Remove archive maintenance | Yes | No | No |
| Remove successor training | Yes | No | No |
| Capture evaluator and admission standard | No | Yes | No |
| Corrupt both discovery and checking observations | No | No | Yes |

Here competent succession means actual transfer of the retained strict-checker program and operating skill; it does not certify the sensor in the corrupted-calibration condition. Carrier labels alternate in a finite turnover abstraction.

The capture result is especially informative: some correct service keeps recurring while harmful responses also occur. Recurrence alone would misclassify it. Correlated corruption produces 122 reachable states with an internally strict but physically false certificate. More checking through the same compromised instrument cannot establish truth.

Across all eight conditions, an independently written graph reader checked **2,455 states and 2,587 transitions**, recomputed physical event meanings and payment identities, and used depth-first cycle detection and computed ranks to verify recurrence. It agrees with the producer. Separate reviews checked the mathematics, observation restrictions, enacted evaluator change, and actual archive contents. These are AI-assisted mathematical and software checks of a synthetic process, not fresh human experiments or proof-assistant certification.

The witness supplies a finite grammar, reliable baseline calibration, within-period stability, continuing productive inputs, and a persistent paid scheduler and auxiliary apparatus. Its training is executable payload transmission. Its evaluator revision concerns simplicity versus evidence fit. Human moral development, the invention of unlimited concepts, and the origin of the apparatus are not demonstrated by those operations. The general framework can represent these questions; each needs its own adequate mechanism and evidence. The [certification report](combined-process-certification.md) records the detailed contract and reproduction instructions.

## What “complete” now means

Three achievements can be asserted together:

1. **An integrated scope:** material support, psychological formation, ethical direction, institutional action, succession, and self-revision fit within one account of changes to future possibilities.
2. **An exact general process characterization:** for a declared actual transition system, the protection-and-recurrence condition is necessary and sufficient; finiteness of the state space is unnecessary.
3. **A checked joint realization:** the bounded executable process satisfies those conditions, with explicit controls showing which mechanisms its success depends on.

The normative direction is already part of this theory: affected parties cannot be excluded merely because the operator benefits from excluding them. Norm revision must address facts, standing, reasons, and existing obligations; changing the success label cannot erase a harm. That direction is openly defended rather than inferred from the fact that some process persists.

This yields concrete grounds for rejecting unreasonable claims: spending the same reserve twice; presenting inaccessible information as usable knowledge; calling unexecuted repair successful; treating a score change as a repaired injury; counting expansion while excluding those whose conditions it destroys; or assuming a successor inherits capacities that were never maintained and transmitted. Which option is best in a difficult conflict can still require substantive judgment.

**The combined operational foundation is established at the stated level.** Calling it the complete fundamental theory of reality would add a further claim: that its substantive mechanisms and interpretation cover every intended domain. Neither the general transition notation nor the textual convergence proves that claim. A Maxwell-like comparison would require comparably specific substantive laws and evidence in a declared domain, alongside this structural foundation.

The foundation is therefore broader and more complete than a theory of financing repair. Its completed contribution is the connection between formation, action, consequences, and the renewal or corruption of the conditions of future action—including the conditions under which that connection succeeds or fails.

Evidence: [reproducible combined-foundation bundle](combined-foundation-evidence.zip). Earlier studies and reference repositories remain unchanged.

# Certifying the combined process, including revision of its controllers

5 October 2026. This is a compositional certificate and an exact semantic characterization for a declared installed process. The state set may be infinite. Controllers, representations, evaluators, permissions, records, and successors can change through that process. The result does not assume that a successful policy is automatically selected or installed, and it does not identify continuing production with universal goodness.

This note extends the two-way representation contract in [completeness bridge](completeness-bridge.md), the installed-process distinction in the theories workspace's `closure-study/FORMAL.md`, the local-dependency result in `generative-basis/formal/STRUCTURAL-CLOSURE.md`, and the paid revision certificate R6.1 from the structural-foundations cycle 6. The proof methods are standard invariant, well-foundedness, and transition-system arguments; no mathematical-priority claim is made.

## 1. The object is the actual joint process

Let Z be a set of configurations. It need not be finite, countable, or bounded in the length of represented programs. A configuration can contain:

\[
z=(x,\mu,c,m,r,g,e,\theta,a,b,\ell,p).
\]

Here x is the plant/environment condition; μ the operative mechanism or interpreter configuration; c the installed controller code; m its actual working memory; r stored observations and evidence; g the available candidate expressions or programs; e the evaluator/checker configuration; θ the current represented evaluative commitments; a permissions and execution gates; b a joint resource ledger; ℓ carrier/training/succession state; and p the actual protocol phase and event/obligation monitors. These are roles, not a mandatory ontology or a claim that all real systems possess all these registers.

The installed joint transition relation is

\[
z\xrightarrow{\gamma}z',
\tag{1}
\]

where γ records the actual microstep's delivered events, resource transfers, and elapsed time. Equation (1) includes the outcomes of the **installed** code under every admitted environmental outcome. It is not an existential choice of a better external controller. If several actors act, their individual proposal maps must each use that actor's permitted observation and memory; the joint relation then describes their actual interaction. This allows analysis of a fixed decentralized institution without claiming a general decentralized synthesis algorithm.

Each actor's proposal distribution is equal at histories with the same permitted observation and installed internal state, including the operative code, parameters, and memory. A hidden full state can be used by the analyst when defining (1); it cannot be an undeclared argument of a participant's rule. If randomness or a coordinating signal affects proposal selection, its availability and joint law are part of the interface. A rule label must actually change later action selection when changed; adding an unused “endogenous evaluator” field is not a mechanism.

Use physical microsteps whenever internal phases matter. A macrostep may stand in for them only after its every-prefix contract has been proved. This includes sensing, inference, checking, admission, actual execution, replenishment, code copying, report retention, training, installation, and evaluator or commitment revision.

**Totality and termination.** We require at least one admitted actual successor from every continuing configuration. Unavailable actions, denied permissions, exhausted funds, interpreter errors, and deadlocks must have explicit outcomes. A deadlock is a losing sink for a continuing-duty specification unless the stated objective permits termination. Legitimate completion, authorized refusal, or exit can instead have a terminal outcome accepted by a finite duty. Representing that outcome by an absorbing formal state does not claim continuing physical activity.

## 2. Specify duties independently of self-reported success

Let K⊆Z be the declared acceptable configuration set. K may include recoverable error, rest, suspended inquiry, and bounded revision. It excludes only the independently stated violations: an actual cash shortfall, an unexecuted deadline obligation, a prohibited physical harm, falsified provenance, or another specified outcome. No universal ranking of those concerns is derived here.

The institution's score, label of success, or represented norm θ is separately recorded. Revision of θ may be legitimate, but a score change alone does not change a recorded physical outcome or prove that another person's standing has been protected. There are two different contracts:

1. Preserve a stated physical/relational protection envelope while revising forecasts, weights, procedures, or subsidiary criteria inside it.
2. Permit the protection specification itself to change according to an explicitly supplied revision procedure, with versioned commitments, standing, reasons, and treatment of existing obligations.

The second is a trace-level specification of legitimate revision, not a derivation that the current regime's preferred criterion is correct. Add the required history or finite/unbounded monitor to Z. Historical harm and already incurred obligations cannot disappear merely because a later register uses different words. If the user elects to change the external analytical specification, report it as a changed question.

For a continuing duty, let E₁,…,E_q be independently interpreted **transition events**. Examples are delivered service, completed maintenance, a successor actually receiving usable competence, or an effective response to a registered challenge. Repeatedly visiting a state labelled “can revise” is not repeated revision. A reported event must correspond to its actual physical condition. The safety-plus-recurrence property is

\[
\forall t\ge0:\ z_t\in K,
\qquad
\forall j\le q:\ E_j(\gamma_t)\text{ occurs infinitely often}.
\tag{2}
\]

Require recurrence only where the stated duty warrants it. A theory can explain a good rest, completed task, proper refusal, or legitimate ending. It need not require every module to run forever or every evaluator to change continually.

## 3. Exact safety on arbitrary state sets

For a totalized relation Δ induced by (1), define

\[
F(A)=K\cap\{z:\Delta(z)\subseteq A\}.
\]

The greatest fixed point

\[
W=\nu A\,F(A)
\tag{3}
\]

exists by monotonicity on the powerset lattice. For any initial configuration, membership in W is equivalent to every actual admitted run remaining in K. More generally, an initial set B is safe exactly when B⊆W.

**Proof.** W⊆K and Δ(W)⊆W, so induction preserves K along every run. Conversely let A be all configurations reachable from B. If all actual runs are safe, every finite reachable prefix is in K, so A⊆K, and reachability gives Δ(A)⊆A. Thus A is post-fixed for F and A⊆W. This uses the explicit serial/termination convention so a finite bad or deadlocked execution is not erased from the run semantics. ∎

This is an exact characterization of the installed process, not an optimizer. No maximization over hypothetical replacement rules appears in (3). If the installed institution declines a viable repair, that refusal is an actual edge and may defeat the property.

The theorem does not supply a terminating algorithm on arbitrary infinite Z. Ordinary finite fixed-point iteration is available when the full model and relevant distinctions are finite and effective. On arbitrary sets, transfinite characterization or another proof may be necessary.

## 4. Exact safety and recurring progress through well-founded ranks

A relation is *forward well-founded* here when it admits no infinite forward chain. In ordinary set theory with dependent choice, this is equivalent to the usual well-foundedness of the inverse relation and permits an ordinal-valued rank that strictly decreases along forward edges.

For A⊆Z and each event E_j, form the no-event relation

\[
R_j=\{(z,z')\in A^2:\exists\gamma,
\ z\xrightarrow{\gamma}z'\ \land\neg E_j(\gamma)\}.
\tag{4}
\]

The existential γ matters: if the same pair of endpoints can arise both with and without the delivered event, the no-event edge remains. Endpoint equality alone cannot certify event delivery.

**Theorem C — exact installed-process characterization.** Under the stated totality/termination convention and ordinary well-founded recursion, all actual runs from B satisfy (2) **if and only if** there is a set A and, for each required event j, a rank ρ_j:A→Ord such that:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&B\subseteq A\subseteq K,\\
&z\in A\land z\xrightarrow{\gamma}z'\quad\Longrightarrow\quad z'\in A,\\
&z\in A\land z\xrightarrow{\gamma}z'\land\neg E_j(\gamma)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \rho_j(z')<\rho_j(z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

Ranks may reset or increase when the corresponding actual event occurs. They are mathematical witnesses, not free inputs available to the controller.

**Sufficiency.** The first two lines give safety by induction. If E_j occurred only finitely often on a run, its suffix after the last occurrence would have a strictly decreasing infinite ordinal rank, which is impossible. Hence every required event recurs. This argument applies separately to each j, under the same actual joint process. It does not splice together different successful controllers. ∎

**Necessity.** Let A be the states reachable from B, including actual controller memory, installed code, pending obligations, and any history needed for the transition semantics. Safety gives A⊆K and reachability gives closure. If R_j had an infinite forward chain, prepend a finite run from B to its first state and choose the corresponding no-event transition for each chain edge. This would give an admitted run with only finitely many E_j events, contradicting (2). R_j is therefore forward well-founded. Define by well-founded recursion

\[
\rho_j(z)=\sup\{\rho_j(z')+1:(z,z')\in R_j\}.
\tag{6}
\]

Because A is a set, the successor ranks form a set of ordinals and the supremum exists. Equation (6) strictly decreases on each no-event edge, providing (5). ∎

For state-labelled progress P_j, this yields the familiar form: the relation restricted to A∖P_j is well-founded, with a rank decreasing on transitions that stay outside P_j. Entry into P_j resets progress. Actual event monitors are preferable when the outcome is a delivered action rather than a standing state property.

**Finite case.** If A is finite, R_j must be acyclic. The length of the longest no-event path from a state supplies a natural-number rank, bounded by |A|−1. Checking these ranks or the equivalent absence of an event-free cycle certifies **sure** recurrence. This is stronger than a finite Markov chain's probability-one recurrence, which may allow a probability-zero path that delays the event forever.

**Why ordinals are useful.** Infinite state does not require finite ranks. A node may branch to countdowns of every finite length and still have no infinite event-free path; its ordinal rank can be ω. There is no uniform finite completion bound in that example. The theorem consequently characterizes eventual recurrence without incorrectly supplying bounded latency.

The necessity construction is semantic: it does not purport to compute a rank from every program. The usable noncircular certificate is the sufficiency direction, where a concrete invariant and rank are supplied independently and checked against the actual local transitions. Taking A to mean “the successful states” without discharging those checks is not a certification procedure.

## 5. Local contracts that certify the whole rather than assume it

Decompose the actual microstep relation into declared component relations Δ_i selected by real guards or phases. A component may be formation, evidence acquisition, checking, admission, execution, maintenance, teaching, succession, or revision. Synchronous joint events can be one component. The relations must cover every actual allowed step, including environmental interference, denial, error, and fallback.

Choose an independently defined joint invariant

\[
H(z)=H_{\rm plant}\land H_{\rm funds}\land H_{\rm records}
\land H_{\rm authority}\land H_{\rm code}\land H_{\rm succession}
\land H_{\rm duty}.
\tag{7}
\]

This decomposition is illustrative. It can be a phase-indexed disjunction of local assertions rather than a conjunction that all phases satisfy identically. Establish:

1. **Initial coverage.** Every declared initial uncertainty state satisfies H. Assumptions about initial code, endowment, records, authority, and skills appear here.
2. **Actual dispatch and nonblocking.** On H the installed proposal/dispatch mechanism selects only declared components, according to available information, and every selected component has a defined nonempty outcome set. A denial is an outcome, not a deleted branch.
3. **Local preservation.** For every component i and actual state satisfying H and its selection guard, every Δ_i outcome satisfies H. If a component is a macrostep, all intermediate states also satisfy the relevant physical/payment protections.
4. **Local progress.** For each required event j, every Δ_i outcome without E_j strictly lowers the chosen well-founded rank. An emitted E_j must satisfy the physical event interpretation, not merely set a flag.
5. **Complete interaction accounting.** Shared resource transfers, shared noise, permissions, hidden guards, and interference used in any local proof agree with the same joint process.
6. **Time contract.** For indefinite physical operation, elapsed time along infinite admitted runs diverges. Bounds on latency require corresponding duration bounds, not just step counts.

Then H and the ranks satisfy Theorem C's sufficient conditions. This is a composition theorem because each component is proved from the current joint invariant and its actual step semantics; global continuation follows by induction and well-foundedness. None of the component proofs is allowed to assume that another component “will always rescue” it without that rescue and its schedule being represented in the transition relation and rank.

A cycle of dependencies is not logically circular. Maintenance can sustain inquiry; inquiry can produce useful proposals; executed proposals can restore maintenance resources. Initial coverage supplies a base case and each actual step preserves the joint assertions. What would be circular is assuming perpetual maintenance in the inquiry proof and perpetual inquiry in the maintenance proof without proving either from an initially valid state and their actual transitions.

For asynchronous interleavings, include the actual scheduler. A scheduler that may starve a required component forever usually defeats the rank condition. An adequate scheduler realization can establish progress on every path of the resulting relation. Alternatively, explicitly restricting executions by a fairness assumption requires a separate fair-liveness argument: Theorem C characterizes every path of the actual relation, and deleting unfair infinite paths alone does not supply its rank certificate. Do not prove an unconditional all-path theorem by quietly discarding unfair paths.

### Shared funds and interference

Use one ledger per actual resource, with nonnegative balances and transfer identities at every payment prefix. Two modules cannot each spend the same reserve merely because each is separately affordable. Receipts are available only after the transition that delivers them. A promise, a forecast, future output, an unapplied grant, and cash already transferred to a successor are distinct states.

A module must preserve the other modules' needed facts or explicitly transform them into compatible successor facts. Read/write footprints and frame conditions are useful sufficient checks; relying on them requires verifying that hidden guards and selectors do not read omitted variables. Coupled simultaneous updates require a joint proof. Two separately correct marginal transition laws need not preserve a joint harm event when disturbances are correlated.

### Formation, checking, and admission

Candidate generation is the actual mapping from available records, grammar, memory, and resources to proposed code. It need not enumerate all possible meanings. Its output contract records exactly which candidates it can produce and what the succeeding checker can evaluate. A candidate existing in the analyst's hypothesis class is not enough.

Checking consumes real evidence and resources. An accepted report's semantic force must be proved for the declared evidence model. A statistical score with nonzero false acceptance cannot be silently promoted to an all-branch truth guarantee. Safety can instead be maintained by a verified execution envelope/fallback, with statistical usefulness certified separately. Admission requires the available authority, actual installation, and retained runnable payload. An acceptance bit without installation is not a delivered correction.

Maintenance must restore the conditions the next round actually uses. Succession must transfer sufficient program, records, rights, skills, and working resources. An abstract identity of the successor's name or a “copy successful” flag does not prove competent operation. These obligations close the route between modules rather than just show that good endpoints exist.

## 6. Mechanisms and evaluators can revise themselves inside the certificate

Z can contain code strings, interpreters, representations, candidate grammars, evaluative parameters, and validation procedures that change at runtime. The theorem does not require these registers to remain constant. It requires that the actual revision transitions satisfy the same state and progress obligations as any other component.

There are constructive ways to discharge that obligation:

- Admit only programs from a grammar with proved preservation rules.
- Verify finite candidate programs over an explicitly finite local contract.
- Require proof-carrying updates checked by an implemented sound verifier.
- Restrict the actions of an uncertain new controller through a separately certified execution envelope, while allowing the controller's predictions and proposals to change.

These are examples, not mutually exclusive necessities. A verifier that accepts a supplied proof still needs physical computation, memory, installation authority, and an actual soundness argument. A stored certificate is not magically true because the state calls it a certificate.

If the verifier, norm-review procedure, or interpreter itself may change, its update must also preserve the contract governing later steps. Formally, the quantification in local preservation ranges over every reachable μ, c, e, and θ, including newly generated ones. This is not an infinite tower of external governors: it is one transition system containing the governors' physical states. It does retain a declared mathematical interpretation and a proof obligation for the whole admitted mechanism family. Self-revision does not prove that the interpretation is empirically correct from nowhere.

No fixed finite menu of programs is required for the theorem. An unbounded typed syntax and growing records can be included in an infinite Z; closure can be proved by structural induction on generated programs. But a claim to cover every future meaningful concept requires an additional adequacy argument. New syntax alone does not manufacture new physical actions or a correct meaning for its symbols.

### Dependency closure beyond finite state

For a declared coordinate set I and mode-specific old-state read dependencies, begin with the coordinates determining the protected outcomes, permitted observations, permissions, and required monitors. Define

\[
R_{n+1}=R_n\cup\bigcup_{i\in R_n,\lambda}\operatorname{Pa}_i^\lambda,
\qquad R_* =\bigcup_{n<\omega}R_n.
\tag{8}
\]

Even when I is infinite, R_* is the least parent-closed set containing the seed. If i∈R_*, it is in some R_n, so all its parents are in R_{n+1}; every other closed set contains all R_n by induction. Thus finiteness is needed for finite termination of the closure algorithm, not for this leastness result.

For dynamically selected mechanisms, the dependency list must include the selector/code reads or conservatively cover every admitted mechanism. Such closure may expand to all of I and may be infinite or noncomputable. If the update functions and shared fresh-noise contract meet the structural theorem's hypotheses, equal retained states and common noise still give equal retained successor states coordinate by coordinate. Measurability is additionally required for probability-law claims on infinite products. This is representation closure; it does not prove that the retained process is safe or recurrent. Theorem C supplies that separate dynamical obligation.

## 7. Duties allowing rest, resolution, and legitimate exit

The combined architecture should not turn `GF production` into the definition of a good process. For a response duty, a more appropriate specification is

\[
\mathbf G(\text{request }r\Rightarrow\mathbf F\text{resolution }r).
\tag{9}
\]

Create an actual monitored obligation token when r is admitted. It can be discharged only by the specified resolution—possibly successful work, an authorized refusal with the required reasons and protections, or a legitimate exit—not by deleting the record.

A sufficient certificate assigns a well-founded rank to every active token, decreasing on each transition during which that token remains unresolved. Token removal must itself satisfy the resolution contract. Then no token remains pending forever. Multiple overlapping requests need token-specific accounting; completing a stream of easy new requests must not conceal an old unfulfilled one.

For a single outstanding obligation, a monitor can track whether it is pending. Recurring return to a nonpending state represents repeated resolution only if genuine resolution clears the monitor and the cleared condition is represented as a distinguishable state before any replacement request. If one transition resolves an old token and admits a new one, the pending bit may remain true even though each token is resolved; use actual resolution events or token-specific ranks in that case. If there are no requests, rest is permitted and no manufactured production is demanded. Deadlines can instead use age counters and make overdue tokens violations of K.

An accepted finite completion state may be absorbing in the mathematical model. This satisfies a completed finite duty, not an assertion of inexhaustible generation. Evaluating that case under an inappropriate recurring-production objective would answer the wrong question.

## 8. Stochastic progress is a separate useful extension

The exact ordinal characterization above concerns **every admitted path**. A process with random retries can have an event-free infinite path of probability zero and therefore fail sure recurrence while succeeding with probability one.

For a stochastic extension, take a well-defined actual joint path law (for example a measurable kernel on a standard Borel configuration space) with H almost-surely invariant. Suppose that, at every admitted history in H, the conditional probability of delivering event E_j within the next L_j microsteps is at least ε_j>0. This bound must include the installed scheduler, memory, code revision, shared funds, and environmental regime; it cannot be an average across histories that hide a failing subgroup.

Then the probability of no E_j during n successive L_j-step windows is at most `(1−ε_j)^n`, without independence. Conditioning successively proves the bound. Its limit is zero, so after every fixed time another E_j occurs almost surely. A countable union over starting times shows E_j recurs infinitely often with probability one. The same argument handles finitely or countably many declared event types by intersection of probability-one events. A uniform positive lower bound on step durations, or another time-divergence argument, is still needed for physical-time recurrence; merely positive durations can sum to a finite time.

This is a sufficient stochastic progress condition, not an exact algorithm for arbitrary kernels. If an irreversible unacceptable outcome retains a uniform positive conditional risk at infinitely many opportunities, infinite-horizon protection can instead have probability zero. Neither an empirical sample with no failures nor small finite-horizon error automatically proves a zero-risk invariant.

## 9. Concrete certification contract for the 23-phase combined witness

The checked executable witness has physical phases 0,…,22; each baseline transition advances to the next phase. It combines paid acquisition, candidate formation, fresh paid checking, evaluator amendment, regeneration, admission, actual execution, maintenance, training, succession, and an adversarial change between complete rounds. Environmental truth remains stable within a round under the declared contract, and changes at the round boundary. Both the stability interval and the sustaining fallback receipts are explicit assumptions of this constructed system.

For an event emitted on source phase p, use

\[
\rho_p(z)=(p-\operatorname{phase}(z))\bmod23.
\tag{10}
\]

Every baseline non-event transition lowers this natural rank by one. At phase p the event must actually occur, and the rank can reset from 0 to 22. If a control advances through phase p without delivering the required event, (5) fails: the non-event edge increases the rank. A stalled non-event phase also fails strict decrease. This catches missing event delivery rather than crediting a printed schedule.

The code checker should establish at least:

| Initial uncertainty | Every declared initial truth table, installed program, evaluator, and reserve is covered |
| Information | Actions depend only on phase, allowed linked records, installed evaluator/memory, and permitted public values |
| Funds | All microstep debits are payable; receipts are delivered at their stated phase; no duplicated resource or free report carry |

Nor does this small grammar establish discovery of arbitrary unrepresented concepts. It demonstrates an actual closed composition of the listed roles, subject to the explicit resource and environmental contract.

## 10. What this closes

The joint-process result goes beyond a collection of independently viable ingredients. It gives an exact safety/recurring-event criterion on arbitrary declared state sets, and local, checkable sufficient conditions for an installed mechanism whose controllers, evaluators, records, and carriers are themselves produced and revised inside the process.

The order of work is concrete: specify local mechanisms and their interpretation; derive the relevant boundary; prove initial coverage; verify every actual component and interference step; verify actual progress or request-resolution ranks; then compose. A positive result certifies the combined process. A failed condition identifies an uncovered input, resource prefix, observation distinction, installation step, revision, or no-progress loop.

This does not require global nontermination of everything, infinite novelty, universal moral agreement, or an unrestricted terminating evaluator. It also does not establish empirical coverage by naming a complete state space. Extending the certificate to a new substantive setting requires its mechanism, observation, resource, outcome, and disturbance correspondence. Cross-tradition accounts can guide which dependencies and failure mechanisms deserve investigation, but textual resemblance alone does not discharge those correspondence obligations or identify distinct ontologies.

# An integrated mechanism of scientific change

## What is now implemented

The remaining integration is implemented as one continuing, bounded community. Ordinary work produces outcomes and income. Observed shortfalls can open a paid investigation. A council can change whose outcomes count in the institutional mandate. A fresh comparison can change the method and the predictor actually used. All of this draws on the same cash account as the maintenance and rebuilding of the checking facility.

This supplies an executable example of the proposed mechanism. It does not establish that the mechanism explains all scientific change, that its particular institutions are desirable, or that it is historically novel. The broader argument and relationship to existing work remain in [Mechanisms of scientific change](mechanisms-of-scientific-change.md).

The core proposition is now more precise: **a community can change the arrangements that determine its next inquiry, while depending on ordinary activity to maintain its ability to investigate those arrangements.** The same feedback can support discovery, delay it, or exhaust the institution's resources.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W[Ordinary work] --> O[Observed outcomes and complaints]
  W --> M[Settled income]
  O --> Q[Decision to open an investigation]
  M --> F[Funding and facility upkeep]
  F --> Q
  Q --> P[Paid construction and pilot]
  P --> G[Council may revise the mandate]
  G --> T[Fresh check under the adopted mandate]
  F --> T
  T --> R[Possible method and predictor change]
  R --> W
```

Every connection in this diagram changes an implemented transition. It is not a diagram of variables whose relationships are left to the reader.

## What the community does

There are two groups, A and B, and one service request from each in every round. Each request has three binary features and a binary outcome. The institution initially evaluates scientific proposals using A's prediction error, although it serves both groups and keeps separate error summaries for both. All scenarios last 700 rounds, so each group has exactly 700 requests whether or not the community can afford to serve them.

Initially, one feature predicts both groups' outcomes. In the lasting-opportunity environment, B's outcome later depends on a relationship between two features: their exclusive-or. Neither feature separately predicts that relationship. A supplied search rule requires a useful single-feature improvement before admitting a combined representation. The proposed edit removes that prerequisite. The candidate is constructed by fitting finite tables; no procedure inserts the correct combined predictor by knowing the world type.

This is a small example of concept construction and admission-rule revision. Its representation grammar, permissible rule edit, and testing procedure are supplied. It does not generate arbitrary scientific languages or revise every higher-level rule.

The community can open a review after a sustained error threshold, a qualifying B complaint, or sufficient time without examining its method, subject to a cooldown and affordability. The last condition is an explicit curiosity policy. The institution receives no hidden phase label or instruction to change methods on the date the environment changes.

An opening reserves the priced construction and pilot stage plus a cash floor. A separate affordability decision follows once the candidate, mandate, and fresh sample size are known. If the full check is unaffordable, the attempt ends without installing the proposed method. Its spent money and review index remain spent.

Ordinary records retain recent group error summaries; they do not retain complete linked feature/outcome records for replay. The checking facility provides the prospective linked records and shadow forecasts required by the implemented review route. It costs money to maintain, can be lost, and can be rebuilt. This establishes dependence on that specified route. It does not prove that every possible alternative form of checking would require the same facility.

## How a purpose changes

The council represents three supplied interests: A, B, and a steward concerned with the worse-served group, operating expense, liquidity, and avoiding observed harm to A. A paid pilot informs their ballots. A majority can give B standing in the mandate, changing its weights from `(A=1, B=0)` to `(A=1/2, B=1/2)`.

That vote changes the criterion used for a subsequent fresh method comparison. It does not itself certify the proposed predictor. Inclusion can therefore precede the money or evidence needed to act on it.

The two sets of group outcomes remain visible throughout. A changing institutional score cannot erase B's previous failures or relabel an unserved request as a correct prediction. The same fresh comparison is also recorded under both sets of weights as a diagnostic; the unused score is not a second retrospectively selected statistical test.

This is endogenous adoption of an institutional purpose among supplied alternatives. The individual concerns, voting constitution, candidate mandates, and valuation of operating cost remain normative inputs. The council is a central representation of those interests, not a population of independently learning political agents. Its pilot-based judgment is fallible, and a successful vote establishes neither ethical legitimacy nor a mathematical discovery of whose interests matter.

## What the checking guarantee actually says

At the start of fresh checking, freeze the actual installed predictor package, the proposed package, the adopted mandate, and the known recurring operating-cost difference `δ`. The task distribution is assumed stationary during that atomic review. One observation round provides one fresh case per group. Both passive predictors can be scored against the same outcome because their forecasts do not cause that outcome; both computations and the required linked records are charged.

Let

\[
G_i=\sum_g w_g\bigl(\mathrm{error}_{\mathrm{installed},g,i}-\mathrm{error}_{\mathrm{candidate},g,i}\bigr)-\delta.
\]

Let `W` be the sum of weights for groups on which the two frozen predictors can disagree on an allowed input. Then `G_i` lies in an interval of width `2W`. The known cost difference shifts that interval without widening it. Review `j` receives

\[
\alpha_j=\frac{0.05}{j(j+1)}.
\]

The sample size is fixed before fresh checking; the code targets a radius of .075 subject to a 64–512 round cap. Acceptance requires

\[
\overline G-2W\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\alpha_j)}{2n}}>0.
\]

Under independent checking draws from the declared stationary review law, Hoeffding's inequality bounds acceptance of a nonpositive-mean proposal by `α_j`, conditional on the prior history and pilot. Conditioning and the union bound extend this to adaptively opened reviews because the allowances sum to .05. Started attempts consume their index even if the pilot fails or the full check is unaffordable. No favorable early prefix can authorize acceptance. If `W=0`, the weighted forecasts agree everywhere and their gain is determined by the known cost difference.

This is a guarantee about the **frozen deployed packages under the current review distribution**. It does not certify the candidate-generating algorithm for all future tasks, the mandate's ethics, or future advantage after drift. Initial bootstrap fitting and the council's pilot-based decision do not receive this outer guarantee. The simulation uses deterministic keyed pseudorandom streams to instantiate the declared draw laws; a fixed tape is not itself a source of mathematical randomness.

One-time research expense is kept in the cash and total program accounts. A positive recurring deployment gain does not imply that the research pays back its total cost. The conversion between operating currency and error in this objective is supplied, not deduced from the theory.

## Material accounting and audit

All named costs draw on the same account: acquisition, field reading, linkage, fitting, forecasts, opening, hearings, checking, ordinary operation, refunds, upkeep, and rebuilding. Cash enters through endowed initial capital and settled service fees. There is no borrowing against future revenue and no unrecorded rescue transfer. Outcomes and fees settle within the service round; a full review is an atomic experiment during which the task law is held stationary. Long research delays, changing prices inside an experiment, and opportunity costs beyond the named tariffs are not modeled.

All **1,920 runs** passed the evaluator's fixed-denominator and cash checks. An independent saved-record audit reconstructed **460 completed package comparisons** and **188 enacted changes**. Every enacted change had positive exact expected gain under its own declared current review law; no nonpositive-gain formal acceptance was found. This is an observed audit result, not a claim of zero theoretical error probability or a .05 error budget shared across all 1,920 institutions.

The pre-freeze instrumentation separately verified payment before every acquired observation and fitted table, chronological cash reconciliation, fresh-stage separation, sample-size and bound arithmetic, and no observation access when funds or capability were missing. Normal and optimized Python produced identical behavioral results. The purpose audit independently checked 9,712 transaction prefixes in matched development runs and verified that enactment, rather than different pilot evidence, changed the operative criterion.

All ten hashed source/protocol/analysis files remained identical after evaluation. The stored first-seed full-policy traces include individual transactions; every other run retains per-round intermediate cash minima, totals, counts, and a transaction hash. The compressed run records preserve failures and unfinished reviews.

The pre-freeze audit corrected an important deployment shortcut: reviews now compare candidates against the predictor actually installed, rather than silently refreshing the incumbent first. It also corrected omitted computation charges, payment side effects hidden inside assertions, and fitting debits that followed the computation. Those corrections are documented with the development changes; they were completed before held-out evaluation.

## Consequences for the proposed theory

The integration supports several conditional claims more sharply than an architectural sketch could:

1. **A field can lack recognized failure while an excluded group suffers.** An accurate incumbent target does not necessarily generate the question that would broaden it. In this model, complaints and protected inquiry access supply a route beyond the current target.
2. **Purpose, evidence, and capacity can change at different times.** Institutional recognition need not wait for deployment, and recognition cannot by itself finance a valid test.
3. **Preserving inquiry is a resource-allocation policy with opportunity costs.** It enables later revision in some environments and can undermine ordinary service in others. The poverty failure is a failure of the modeled policy under its contracts, not a proof that every alternative policy must fail.
4. **Loss of checking capacity need not immediately destroy existing competence.** Already compiled predictors can keep working in a stable environment. What is lost here is a route to further investigation and revision.
5. **Scientific change can remain path-dependent even with a fixed evidence rule.** Earlier spending, authority decisions, and capability loss change which later experiments become feasible. More favorable evidence is only one part of the transition.

The completed result is therefore a bounded, executable candidate mechanism of scientific change. It closes the requested causal loop within its stated variables. Human validation, unrestricted concept formation, strategic institutional conflict, changing ultimate commitments, and the evolution of the review constitution remain outside this model. Those boundaries define the scope of the finished result; they are not concealed assumptions that the integration solved them.

# Revising a decision rule while recovery is still possible

Sixth research cycle, 5 October 2026.

The next formal step is complete: the evaluator itself can now detect a changed condition, retain evidence, and pay to revise its selection rule. **A population can still afford to learn and revise its rule, yet lack enough resources to put the corrected rule into operation.** In the main experiment, paid revision still succeeds at epoch 27; at epoch 28 the evaluator becomes correct but cannot fund a successor. The population under the unchanged evaluator remains alive until epoch 32.

A second result prevents an overly broad interpretation. A differently endowed population can maintain a mixture of rules that works through either environment without identifying which environment it faces. The common constraint concerns an executable response to the duty. Diagnosis is one way to obtain that response; a funded robust alternative can substitute for it.

These are conditional mathematical results and exact constructed examples. They extend the cross-scale account without establishing empirical universality or a general law that successful systems must learn.

## What has changed in the formal account

The previous cycle supplied an evaluator that copied operating rules using early or later evidence. This cycle makes the evaluator's calibration a changing physical state. A query does not directly set that state: its report must survive a handoff, the replacement must be installed, an executable operating program must remain available, and its next carrier must be funded.

The three questions from earlier cycles therefore acquire a fourth:

| Question | What must actually be established |
|---|---|
| Could a response work? | A feasible policy exists under the declared information, access, and resource conditions. |
| Will the current rule choose it? | The implemented controller's actions meet the duty. |
| Can it reach a successor? | Required code, assets, records, and operating reserve survive a funded handoff. |
| Can the rule itself be repaired? | The actual revision path reaches a usable replacement before its support is lost. |

The new [revision certificate](revision-and-scale.md) makes the last statement precise. A supplied information-consistent controller must keep every physical and financial prefix valid; a decreasing finite rank ensures that revision finishes; its endpoint must enter a class where the installed controller actually sustains the declared duty. The rank belongs to the proof, not to an unpriced oracle inside the controller.

This is a sufficient certificate, not a claim that every possible adaptation has this form. A known good endpoint alone cannot certify the route to it.

The [population experiment](evaluator-revision.md) retains the actual S and L programs from the previous repair model. S plans one cycle ahead and installs two diagnostic channels. L plans two cycles ahead and installs four. Their operating cash after two cycles remains 100 and 136, respectively.

\[

before extra query/rewrite bills and treasury spill. Here `Φ=260N+R` is a bookkeeping measure of replacement funding, not literal cash. The child's 240-unit cash endowment remains a transfer in the separate cash account.

## More accurate belief can produce worse execution

The separate [noisy-evidence model](paid-revision.md) removes the perfect-report assumption for a finite handoff. It does not insert a noisy detector into the population process. Its own likelihoods, fees, reserves, and deadline are separately specified.

The environment is equally likely to require rule A or B. Each paid signal indicates the correct regime with probability three quarters, independently conditional on that regime. A finite counter retains the evidence. Switching from the current A rule to B takes additional cash and time; a usable successor also needs six units left over.

A supplied three-probe majority rule identifies the right label with probability `27/32`, about 84.4%. With enough reserve and time, it delivers the usable successor at that rate. But at reserve twelve, its observations consume six and a B revision would leave only four for the child. Its usable-delivery probability falls to `27/64`, about 42.2%—below the 50% achieved by simply keeping A.

A controller that includes execution costs in its objective takes one probe in that state and succeeds with probability 75%. An exact decision calculation, exhaustive policy enumeration, and an independent analytical bound agree. Under the stated three-probe grammar, the optimal success probability is:

\[
V(R,D)=
\begin{cases}
27/32,&R\ge14,\ D\ge4,\\
3/4,&R\ge10,\ D\ge2\text{ and the first case fails},\\
1/2,&\text{otherwise, for }R\ge6.
\end{cases}
\]

The improvement concerns a declared probability of funded, timely delivery. Because the base noisy reports overlap between regimes, no finite policy in this grammar guarantees success on every admitted report sequence. This distinction matters when connecting learning to earlier sure-continuation results.

This is a different initial population and an additional admitted allocation rule. It is not a demonstrated no-query recovery from the original two L parents with treasury zero. For a longer protocol, this local intersection is insufficient: later information, memory, and financing must remain compatible along the whole route. The revision certificate checks that additional obligation.

## What carries across scale

The recurring constraint is now more specific than a requirement to preserve resources or acquire knowledge. A declared continuing duty needs a funded, timely route from the present configuration to its next required configuration. Information, diverse alternatives, shared reserves, inherited apparatus, and revision authority can complement or substitute for one another, but only through actual available mechanisms.

Scaling changes these mechanisms. A larger population can support integer mixtures unavailable to one carrier and share a fixed inspection or archive bill. It also requires more birth capital. The mixed control does not make size automatically beneficial; its founding support and allocator are explicit.

An exact scale correspondence must include the environmental change and the **whole revision path**: signal access, retention, interpretation, expense, delay, available code, installation, and successor finance. Correspondences between the settled old and new systems alone do not establish a correspondence between their transitions. Matching final accuracy or average expense can conceal different probabilities of reaching a usable endpoint.

This supports the original direction in a qualified form: the same operational constraints can recur across scales while predicting different outcomes because the affordable response sets and their implementation differ. Universal empirical applicability still requires independently measured mechanisms and tested mappings.
